rv.q: Oil Lamp Theater’s well-paced Poor Behavior succeeds because every element - Rebeck’s incisive writing, Katz’s sharply attuned direction, and a quartet of deeply committed performances - works together to illuminate the muddled, contradictory ways people love, wound, and misread one another.
This play, like marriage itself, is definitely not for the faint of heart.
I found myself drawn to the power of the performances and that each character was real with emotions that were meaningful.

cn.t: Rebeck's tense thriller exposes the messy dynamics of two childless couples as their friendship unravels during a country getaway. Critics praise the honest, edge-of-your-seat exploration of marriage's pitfalls.
